questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.topic: A letter to a paper: who it is for
questions.learningObjective: Identify the intended audience of a letter to a paper
questions.stem: Cartographer's projection notes a letter to the editor written in dense technical jargon.

options.text: The letter is for specialists, because the jargon targets experts.
The letter is for the general public, because it is in a paper.
The letter is for officials, because it addresses a paper.
The letter is for no one, because jargon excludes all.

questions.explanation: Dense technical jargon signals the letter is aimed at specialists, not the general readership of the paper. The public reading equates venue with audience.
questions.hint: Match jargon to audience.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.topic: A notice that assumes an audience it lacks
questions.learningObjective: Spot a notice assuming an audience it lacks
questions.stem: Cartographer's projection notes a notice posted in a lobby that assumes readers know the building code.

options.text: The notice suits its audience, because it is posted publicly.
The notice assumes an audience it lacks, because the public may not know the code.
The notice is jargon-free, because it is short.
The notice is confidential, because it is posted in a lobby.

questions.explanation: A public lobby notice that assumes knowledge of the building code addresses an audience it does not have. The suitability reading equates posting with suitability.
questions.hint: Check whether readers have the assumed knowledge.
